# CLAUDE.md

Guidance for Claude Code when working in `apps/commander-recommender/`.

## What this is

A Commander recommender: paste or upload a card list, get ranked Commander suggestions —
including Partner/Background pairs — with cited synergies, ban-list legality, and an estimated
Bracket. React 19 + Vite client (Zustand + TanStack Query/Table), Express 5 + better-sqlite3
server, no ORM. Card data is Scryfall's Oracle Cards bulk export, imported into SQLite at
build/deploy time — the running server never calls Scryfall live.

Read [`../../docs/commander-recommender.md`](../../docs/commander-recommender.md) first — it's
this app's own handoff document (moved here during the monorepo consolidation, file map kept
current) and covers the deeper "why" behind the stack choices, the scoring model, and known risk
areas in more depth than this file repeats. This file is about how to work in the code, not what
the code does. The root [`CLAUDE.md`](../../CLAUDE.md) covers workspace-wide commands and
conventions this file doesn't repeat.

## Commands

Run from `apps/commander-recommender/` unless noted (or use `pnpm --filter mtg-recommender-client`
/ `--filter mtg-recommender-server` from the repo root).

- `pnpm --filter mtg-recommender-client dev` and `pnpm --filter mtg-recommender-server dev`, or
  both via `pnpm dev` from the repo root — API on `:4000`, Vite client on `:5173` (proxies `/api`)
- `cd server && pnpm run prepare-data` — downloads Scryfall's Oracle Cards bulk file and seeds
  `server/data/cards.sqlite`; required before `/api/recommend` returns anything but a 503. Needs
  network access; reuses a copy less than a week old unless run as `prepare-data:fresh`
- `cd server && pnpm run typecheck` (`tsc`) / `pnpm run build` (`tsc -p tsconfig.build.json`,
  `src/` only, test files excluded — see the note in `tsconfig.build.json` about why `rootDir`
  matters here) / `pnpm test` (Vitest, 12 files colocated under `src/services/`)
- `cd client && pnpm run typecheck` (`tsc -b`) / `pnpm run build` (`tsc -b && vite build`) /
  `pnpm test` (Vitest, 5 files colocated under `src/lib/`)
- `pnpm run lint` in either — no type-aware rules (see `packages/config/eslint.base.js`)
- Single test file: `pnpm exec vitest run src/services/synergy.test.ts` (or any other), from
  whichever of `client`/`server` it lives in

## Architecture

- **`server/src/services/synergy.ts`** is the heart of the app: builds a `CollectionProfile` from
  the matched cards (color identity, creature types, keywords, oracle-text theme regexes), then
  scores every `CommanderUnit` from `partners.ts` against it. A signal counts only once it clears
  `MIN_SIGNAL_COUNT` (3) distinct supporting cards _after_ narrowing to that unit's color identity.
  Kindred requires the unit's own text to _care_ about a type (`caresAboutCreatureType`), not
  merely have it. Color identity gates eligibility and contributes nothing to score — see the
  "scoring measures focus" tests in `synergy.test.ts` before changing the weight formula.
- **`server/src/services/signals.ts`** (879 lines, the largest file) is the signal/role model
  feeding `synergy.ts`: what a card contributes to a deck's plan (`is`/`produces`/`consumes`/
  `rewards`/`amplifies`) and in what capacity. **Read
  [`../../docs/archetypes.md`](../../docs/archetypes.md) before changing this file** — it is the
  reviewable catalog of what those roles and archetypes are _meant_ to mean, derived from twenty real
  decks, and it records which current behaviours are deliberate (so they don't get "fixed") and which
  are known gaps. `deckAnalysis.ts` + `lifecycle.ts` + `packages.ts`
  build on it to answer "what is this list trying to do, and what's it missing" independent of any
  commander — see `docs/commander-recommender.md`'s file map for how those three fit together.
- **`server/src/services/partners.ts`** builds every legal `CommanderUnit` (rule 702.124: one card
  or a legal pair) from the eligible pool — a `CommanderUnit` is what `synergy.ts` scores, not a
  bare `CardRow`. Grouped by ability variant (Partner, Partner—[text], Partner with [Name], Friends
  forever, Choose a Background, Doctor's companion) rather than a cross-product.
- **`server/src/services/eligibility.ts`** judges commander eligibility on a card's **front face

  this can't just substring-match the whole thing. `split` is the deliberate exception (CR 709.4).

  old eligibility until re-imported.

  `services/cardDTO.ts` (`toCardDTO`), shared with `routes/recommend.ts` rather than duplicated.

  Zustand store's split above was designed for. Its `basepath` reads `import.meta.env.BASE_URL` at

- **`client/src/lib/mtg.ts`** — WUBRG ordering and color-identity naming ("Golgari", never

## Conventions

- Comments explain _why_, not _what_ — match the existing tone (see `synergy.ts`'s comments on the
  scoring formula, or `eligibility.ts`'s on front-face-only reasoning).
- Keep changes proportional to the ask. This codebase deliberately favors a short, readable
  heuristic over a "complete" system in synergy detection and Bracket estimation — see
  `docs/commander-recommender.md`'s "Core logic" section before making one more sophisticated.
- Match the existing pattern for whichever file you're touching. If the surrounding code uses a
  plain function and a `Set`, don't reach for a class or a new dependency to do the same job.
- **Never write oracle text from memory — copy it from the database.** Scryfall has moved much
  self-referential wording from a card's name to "this creature"/"this land"; two rules in this
  codebase were written from recall and were wrong on real cards (see
  `docs/commander-recommender.md`'s "Known risk areas"). Every string in `signals.test.ts` is
  copied verbatim from the imported database — keep it that way.
- Before opening a PR: typecheck and test both `client/` and `server/`, and actually run the app
  for anything user-visible — a clean typecheck and passing tests are necessary, not sufficient
  (they don't catch a CSS rule that silently stopped applying, for instance).
- Add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry under `[Unreleased]` for any user-facing change, in the existing
  style (see `1.7.1`'s entry for the level of detail expected).
- `docs/commander-recommender.md`'s file map is meant to stay current — update it in the same
  commit whenever you add, rename, or remove a file it lists.

134:  * `findCounterKind`. `gameState` is further out — see
135:  * docs/signals-rework.md's Phase B status note.

250: /**
251:  * Removes the card's own name from its oracle text.
252:  *
253:  * A card's rules text refers to itself by name, so any check that regexes a
254:  * word against oracle text will match that word for free when it appears in
255:  * the name. Goblin Sharpshooter's abilities are "doesn't untap", "whenever a
256:  * creature dies, untap" and a ping — it does not care about Goblins in the
257:  * slightest — yet it matched Goblin kindred purely because "Goblin" is in its
258:  * name. Names are not abilities, so they are removed before anything reads
259:  * the text.
260:  *
261:  * Both the full name and the pre-comma short form go, since rules text uses
262:  * the short form ("Lathril" for "Lathril, Blade of the Elves").
263:  */
264: export function stripSelfReferences(text: string, ...names: (string | null)[]): string {
265:   let out = text;
266:   const forms = new Set<string>();
267:   for (const name of names) {
268:     if (!name) continue;
269:     forms.add(name);
270:     // "Lathril, Blade of the Elves" -> also strip "Lathril".
271:     // .split() on any string always returns at least one element.
272:     const short = name.split(',')[0]!.trim();
273:     if (short && short !== name) forms.add(short);
274:   }
275:   // Longest first, so the full name goes before its own short form.
276:   for (const form of [...forms].sort((a, b) => b.length - a.length)) {
277:     out = out.split(form).join(' ');
278:   }
279:   return out;
280: }

282: /** Every word in a piece of text, lowercased. The unit of vocabulary
283:  * lookup — see `candidateTypes` for why looking up beats searching. */
284: function wordsIn(text: string): string[] {
285:   return text.toLowerCase().match(/[a-z][a-z'-]*/g) ?? [];
286: }

288: /**
289:  * Creature types of tokens this card creates.
290:  *
291:  * Read out of each "create ... token" clause, so a type mentioned elsewhere
292:  * in an unrelated sentence isn't credited as a token type.
293:  */
294: function findProducedTokenTypes(text: string, vocab: Vocabulary): string[] {
295:   const found = new Set<string>();
296:   for (const clause of text.match(/create[^.;]*token[^.;]*/gi) ?? []) {
297:     for (const word of wordsIn(clause)) {
298:       const type = vocab.typeByWord.get(word);
299:       if (type) found.add(type);
300:     }
301:   }
302:   return [...found];
303: }

305: /**
306:  * Creature types this card creates or grows via `amass` — "amass Orcs 1"
307:  * both grows (or creates) an Army token and turns it into the named type, so
308:  * it counts as producing both. The reminder explaining the mechanic is
309:  * stripped like any other, but the keyword's own printed name and type
310:  * argument survive.
311:  */
312: function findAmassedTypes(text: string, vocab: Vocabulary): string[] {
313:   const found = new Set<string>();
314:   for (const match of text.matchAll(/\bamass (\w+)/gi)) {
315:     found.add('Army');
316:     const type = vocab.typeByWord.get(match[1]!.toLowerCase());
317:     if (type) found.add(type);
318:   }
319:   return [...found];
320: }

322: /**
323:  * Lookup tables for the vocabulary signal detection recognises.
324:  *
325:  * Built once and reused across every card. The point is direction: with a
326:  * map, recognising a card's types costs one lookup per word it contains;
327:  * without one, it cost a regex per type in Magic. Across the card pool that
328:  * was the difference between ~8 seconds and ~82.
329:  */
330: export interface Vocabulary {
331:   /** Lowercased word, singular or plural, to its canonical creature type:
332:    * "elves" and "elf" both map to "Elf". */
333:   typeByWord: Map<string, string>;
334:   /** Lowercased single-word keyword to its canonical form. */
335:   keywordByWord: Map<string, string>;
336:   /** Keywords containing a space, which single-word lookup cannot find. */
337:   multiWordKeywords: string[];
338: }
339: 
340: export function buildVocabulary(creatureTypes: string[], keywords: string[]): Vocabulary {
341:   const typeByWord = new Map<string, string>();
342:   for (const type of creatureTypes) {
343:     typeByWord.set(type.toLowerCase(), type);
344:     typeByWord.set(pluralOfType(type).toLowerCase(), type);
345:   }
346: 
347:   const keywordByWord = new Map<string, string>();
348:   const multiWordKeywords: string[] = [];
349:   for (const keyword of keywords) {
350:     if (keyword.includes(' ')) multiWordKeywords.push(keyword);
351:     else keywordByWord.set(keyword.toLowerCase(), keyword);
352:   }
353: 
354:   return { typeByWord, keywordByWord, multiWordKeywords };
355: }

357: const wordPatternCache = new Map<string, RegExp>();

359: function escapeRegExp(value: string): string {
360:   return value.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');
361: }

363: /**
364:  * The English plural of a creature type, because cards refer to a type in the
365:  * aggregate — "Elves you control", not "Elf you control". Only the irregular
366:  * endings Magic's type list actually contains are handled.
367:  */
368: export function pluralOfType(type: string): string {
369:   // Elf -> Elves, Dwarf -> Dwarves. Lathril says "ten untapped Elves you
370:   // control", so missing this drops one of the format's best-known kindred
371:   // commanders.
372:   if (/f$/i.test(type)) return type.replace(/f$/i, 'ves');
373:   // Sphinx -> Sphinxes, Fungus -> Funguses, Leech -> Leeches.
374:   if (/(s|x|z|ch|sh)$/i.test(type)) return `${type}es`;
375:   return `${type}s`;
376: }

378: const tokenDescriptorCache = new Map<string, RegExp>();
379: 
380: /**
381:  * A token's printed type line inside a "create" clause — "Goblin creature
382:  * tokens", "Necron Warrior artifact creature tokens". Any number of
383:  * intervening words, since a token's full type line can carry several
384:  * subtypes and permanent types before "tokens" — one intervening word was
385:  * not enough to strip "Necron Warrior artifact creature tokens", and Their
386:  * Number Is Legion falsely read as a Necron payoff as a result.
387:  */
388: function tokenDescriptorPattern(type: string): RegExp {
389:   let pattern = tokenDescriptorCache.get(type);
390:   if (!pattern) {
391:     const forms = `(?:${escapeRegExp(type)}|${escapeRegExp(pluralOfType(type))})`;
392:     pattern = new RegExp(`\\b${forms}(?:\\s+\\w+)*\\s+(?:creature\\s+)?tokens?\\b`, 'gi');
393:     tokenDescriptorCache.set(type, pattern);
394:   }
395:   // Shared cached regex with /g — reset before each use.
396:   pattern.lastIndex = 0;
397:   return pattern;
398: }
399: 
400: /**
401:  * The card's own text with token-descriptor phrases ("Goblin creature
402:  * tokens") erased, but only *inside* a "create ... token" clause — the
403:  * Krenko's Command case the stripping exists for, mirroring
404:  * `findProducedTokenTypes`'s own clause-scoping. Stripping the same phrase
405:  * everywhere else is wrong: it erased Gleaming Overseer's "Zombie tokens you
406:  * control have hexproof and menace", Eternal Skylord's flying grant, and
407:  * Dreadhorde Invasion's attack trigger, none of which are inside a
408:  * token-creation clause.
409:  */
410: function withoutTokenDescriptors(text: string, type: string): string {
411:   return text.replace(/create[^.;]*token[^.;]*/gi, (clause) =>
412:     clause.replace(tokenDescriptorPattern(type), ' '),
413:   );
414: }

416: /** Matches a word or its plural, on a word boundary. Cached: this runs against
417:  * every candidate in a pool of thousands. */
418: function wordPattern(word: string): RegExp {
419:   let pattern = wordPatternCache.get(word);
420:   if (!pattern) {
421:     pattern = new RegExp(
422:       `\\b(?:${escapeRegExp(word)}|${escapeRegExp(pluralOfType(word))})\\b`,
423:       'i',
424:     );
425:     wordPatternCache.set(word, pattern);
426:   }
427:   return pattern;
428: }

430: /**
431:  * Whether the card sacrifices *itself*, as opposed to an indefinite object.
432:  *
433:  * Two spellings, because Scryfall changed theirs. Older text named the card
434:  * ("Sacrifice Arid Mesa:"); current text says "Sacrifice this land:" /
435:  * "Sacrifice this creature:". Both are read off the RAW text — the
436:  * name-stripped copy renders the first form as a bare "Sacrifice :".
437:  */
438: function detectsSelfSacrifice(rawText: string, names: string[]): boolean {
439:   if (/\bsacrifice this\b/i.test(rawText)) return true;
440:   return names.some((name) => {
441:     // .split() on any string always returns at least one element.
442:     const short = name.split(',')[0]!.trim();
443:     return short !== '' && new RegExp(`sacrifice ${escapeRegExp(short)}\\b`, 'i').test(rawText);
444:   });
445: }

447: /**
448:  * Whether every +1/+1 counter clause on the card targets only itself.
449:  *
450:  * Modeled on `detectsSelfSacrifice`: read off the RAW text, because
451:  * name-stripping destroys the evidence — "put a +1/+1 counter on Kalamax"
452:  * name-stripped is indistinguishable from a counter put on anything. A card
453:  * whose only counter clause grows itself (Kalamax's copy trigger,
454:  * Dragonsguard Elite's Magecraft) is not producing for a +1/+1 Counters
455:  * deck; a card with no counter clause at all trivially does not "grow only
456:  * itself" either.
457:  */
458: function detectsSelfGrowth(rawText: string, names: string[]): boolean {
459:   const counterClauses = clauses(rawText).filter((c) => /\+1\/\+1 counters?/i.test(c));
460:   if (counterClauses.length === 0) return false;
461:   const shortNames = names.map((name) => name.split(',')[0]!.trim()).filter((n) => n !== '');
462:   return counterClauses.every((clause) => {
463:     if (/\bon this (?:creature|permanent)\b/i.test(clause)) return true;
464:     return shortNames.some((short) => new RegExp(`\\bon ${escapeRegExp(short)}\\b`, 'i').test(clause));
465:   });
466: }

468: /** Quantifiers a sacrifice cost is phrased with, beyond the small set the
469:  * catalog used to test for — "one or more", "up to N", and "any number of"
470:  * all pay a real cost, and Plumb the Forbidden ("you may sacrifice one or
471:  * more creatures") matched none of the old set at all. */
472: const SACRIFICE_QUANTIFIER =
473:   'a|an|another|one or more|up to (?:one|two|three|four|five|six|seven|eight|nine|ten|\\d+)|' +
474:   'any number of|two|three|four|five|\\d+|x';
475: 
476: const sacrificeKindCache = new Map<string, RegExp>();
477: 
478: /** Everything before a clause's own `:`, or the whole clause if it has none
479:  * (a spell's additional cost, which is never an activated ability). */
480: function costSideOf(clause: string): string {
481:   const colon = clause.indexOf(':');
482:   return colon === -1 ? clause : clause.slice(0, colon);
483: }

485: /**
486:  * Whether a clause's COST sacrifices an object of the given kind — "a
487:  * creature", "a Zombie", "an artifact", "a token" — not merely mentions it
488:  * somewhere else in the same ability.
489:  *
490:  * Shared by `aristocrats.consumes` and `detectKindred`'s own consumes test,
491:  * which used to disagree about the same sentence in both directions:
492:  * Wilhelt's "you may sacrifice a Zombie" is a Zombie consumer but wasn't
493:  * recognised as a sacrifice outlet at all, because the old aristocrats
494:  * regex required the literal word "creature"; Sophia's "{1}, Sacrifice an
495:  * artifact token: Put a +1/+1 counter on each Dog you control" registered
496:  * as *consuming Dogs*, which she does not, because the old check read the
497:  * whole clause instead of just the cost.
498:  *
499:  * Deliberately excludes "sacrifices" (third person) — "Each player
500:  * sacrifices a creature" is an edict, not an outlet, and must keep failing.
501:  */
502: function sacrificesKind(clause: string, kind: string): boolean {
503:   let pattern = sacrificeKindCache.get(kind);
504:   if (!pattern) {
505:     const forms = `(?:${escapeRegExp(kind)}|${escapeRegExp(pluralOfType(kind))})`;
506:     pattern = new RegExp(`\\bsacrifice (?:${SACRIFICE_QUANTIFIER})\\b.*\\b${forms}\\b`, 'i');
507:     sacrificeKindCache.set(kind, pattern);
508:   }
509:   return pattern.test(costSideOf(clause));
510: }

512: const SACRIFICE_OBJECT_PATTERN = new RegExp(
513:   `\\bsacrifice (?:${SACRIFICE_QUANTIFIER})\\s+([a-z][a-z'-]*)`,
514:   'i',
515: );
516: 
517: /**
518:  * Whether a clause's cost sacrifices a creature — either the bare word
519:  * "creature[s]", or a named creature type the card never spells out
520:  * generically. Krenko's own sacrifice outlets (Goblin Bombardment,
521:  * Siege-Gang Commander, Arms Dealer, Goblin Grenade) all say "Sacrifice a
522:  * Goblin", never the word "creature".
523:  */
524: function sacrificesACreature(clause: string, vocab: Vocabulary): boolean {
525:   if (sacrificesKind(clause, 'creature')) return true;
526:   const match = SACRIFICE_OBJECT_PATTERN.exec(costSideOf(clause));
527:   return !!match && vocab.typeByWord.has(match[1]!.toLowerCase());
528: }

530: const TIME_COUNTER_PATTERN = new RegExp(`\\b(?:${TIME_COUNTER_KEYWORDS.join('|')})\\b`, 'i');
531: const MINUS_ONE_MINUS_ONE_PATTERN = new RegExp(
532:   `\\b(?:${MINUS_ONE_MINUS_ONE_KEYWORDS.map((k) => `${k}(?:s|ed|ing)?`).join('|')})\\b`,
533:   'i',
534: );
535: 
536: /**
537:  * Counter kinds named in the corpus beyond +1/+1 and -1/-1: stun (rule
538:  * 122.1d), lore (Sagas, rule 714), and the LOTR-set kinds — burden, oil,
539:  * corpse, supply, foreshadow, stash, eon, enlightened, loyalty. Each is
540:  * just a name from CR 122.1's glossary of counter types, recognised
541:  * generically ("<name> counter(s)") rather than as its own keyword ability.
542:  */
543: const NAMED_COUNTER_KINDS = [
544:   'stun',
545:   'lore',
546:   'burden',
547:   'oil',
548:   'corpse',
549:   'supply',
550:   'foreshadow',
551:   'stash',
552:   'eon',
553:   'enlightened',
554:   'loyalty',
555: ];
556: 
557: /**
558:  * The specific kind of counter a clause cares about — "+1/+1", "-1/-1",
559:  * "time" (Suspend/Vanishing/Time Travel), "stun", "loyalty", or whatever
560:  * named counter the card itself prints. Counters are a family, not a
561:  * keyword — the corpus alone needs at least a dozen kinds beyond the
562:  * literal string "+1/+1", and most of them (Blight, Persist, Suspend,
563:  * Vanishing) only ever name their counter inside reminder text that's
564:  * already stripped by the time this runs.
565:  *
566:  * Deliberately does NOT fall back to "whatever word precedes 'counter(s)'"
567:  * generically — The Ozolith's "if it had counters on it" would wrongly
568:  * extract "had" as a counter kind. A card that only ever says bare
569:  * "counters" stays unqualified on purpose.
570:  */
571: function findCounterKind(clause: string): string | undefined {
572:   const plusMinus = clause.match(/([+-]\d*\/[+-]\d*)\s+counters?/i);
573:   if (plusMinus) return plusMinus[1];
574:   if (MINUS_ONE_MINUS_ONE_PATTERN.test(clause)) return '-1/-1';
575:   if (TIME_COUNTER_PATTERN.test(clause) || /\btime counters?\b/i.test(clause)) return 'time';
576:   for (const kind of NAMED_COUNTER_KINDS) {
577:     if (new RegExp(`\\b${kind} counters?\\b`, 'i').test(clause)) return kind;
578:   }
579:   return undefined;
580: }

582: /** Every counter kind a card's own text cares about, for `supporterMatches`
583:  * (synergy.ts) to narrow a `counterType`-qualified signal's citable
584:  * supporters the same way it narrows `creatureType`/`keyword`. */
585: function findAllCounterKinds(text: string): string[] {
586:   const found = new Set<string>();
587:   for (const clause of clauses(text)) {
588:     const kind = findCounterKind(clause);
589:     if (kind) found.add(kind);
590:   }
591:   return [...found];
592: }

594: /**
595:  * Whether a clause makes `subject` cheaper or free — "Equipment spells you
596:  * cast cost {1} less", "equip {0}", "pay {0} rather than pay the equip
597:  * cost", "the second spell you cast each turn costs {2} less". Modelled once
598:  * and parameterised by what it reduces, rather than a bespoke regex per
599:  * archetype: Danitha (Aura and Equipment spells), Puresteel Paladin (equip
600:  * {0}), Bruenor Battlehammer (free equip), Bladehold War-Whip (other
601:  * Equipment's own equip cost), and Alisaie Leveilleur's Dualcast (the second
602:  * spell each turn) are all this same shape. Cost reduction is `enables`, not
603:  * `rewards` — it turns the engine on faster, it doesn't reward you for
604:  * having engaged with it.
605:  */
606: function reducesCostOf(text: string, subject: RegExp): boolean {
607:   return clauses(text).some(
608:     (clause) => subject.test(clause) && /costs? \{?\d|pay \{0\}|equip \{0\}/i.test(clause),
609:   );
610: }

612: /**
613:  * The individual face names inside a Scryfall-joined card name
614:  * ("Front // Back" -> ["Front", "Back"]). A single-faced card's name has no
615:  * " // " and splits into just itself.
616:  *
617:  * Needed because oracle text names only the face it belongs to ("Stomp
618:  * deals 2 damage...", never "Bonecrusher Giant // Stomp deals..."), but
619:  * `row.back_name` alone doesn't cover this — it's null for split, adventure,
620:  * and flip layouts (see @mtg/card-model's isTwoSidedLayout, which reserves
621:  * it for transform/modal_dfc only), even though those layouts join their
622:  * stored `name` with " // " the exact same way. Without this, a bare face
623:  * name in oracle text (Bonecrusher Giant's Adventure half, "Stomp") was
624:  * never recognised as a self-reference and so never stripped.
625:  */
626: function faceNamesIn(name: string): string[] {
627:   return name.split(' // ');
628: }

630: /**
631:  * Removes reminder text — the parenthetical restatement of a keyword.
632:  *
633:  * Reminder text explains a keyword the card already has; it is never an
634:  * ability of its own. Leaving it in produced real false positives: Sliver
635:  * Gravemother's Encore reminder text ends "They gain haste", which read as
636:  * the card *granting* haste to your team, i.e. an active Haste payoff.
637:  */
638: function stripReminderText(text: string): string {
639:   return text.replace(/\([^)]*\)/g, ' ');
640: }

642: /**
643:  * Normalises two "lord" templating variants onto the one shape the rest of
644:  * the catalog expects — "<Type> creatures you control get/gain/have" —
645:  * rather than adding a third regex for each archetype that cares.
646:  *
647:  * Older wording omits "you control" ("All Sliver creatures get +1/+1", Muscle
648:  * Sliver); other cards omit "creatures" ("Zombies you control get +1/+1",
649:  * Tomb Tyrant). Functionally identical lords, sorted by which decade the card
650:  * was printed in. Scoped to known creature-type words specifically, so it
651:  * can't misfire on "for each land you control" or similar unrelated phrasing.
652:  */
653: function normalizeLordWording(text: string, vocab: Vocabulary): string {
654:   let out = text.replace(/\ball ([a-z][a-z'-]*) creatures\b/gi, (whole, word: string) =>
655:     vocab.typeByWord.has(word.toLowerCase()) ? `${word} creatures you control` : whole,
656:   );
657:   out = out.replace(
658:     /\b([a-z][a-z'-]*) you control (get|gain|have|gets|gains)\b/gi,
659:     (whole, word: string, verb: string) =>
660:       vocab.typeByWord.has(word.toLowerCase()) ? `${word} creatures you control ${verb}` : whole,
661:   );
662:   return out;
663: }

665: /** The card types a `cardType` qualifier can narrow to — the part of the
666:  * type line before the em dash, supertypes (Legendary, Basic, Snow, World,
667:  * Ongoing) excluded because they say nothing about what the card *is*. */
668: const CARD_TYPES = [
669:   'Creature',
670:   'Instant',
671:   'Sorcery',
672:   'Artifact',
673:   'Enchantment',
674:   'Land',
675:   'Planeswalker',
676:   'Battle',
677:   'Kindred',
678: ];
679: 
680: function findCardTypes(typeLine: string): string[] {
681:   const beforeDash = typeLine.split('—')[0] ?? typeLine;
682:   return CARD_TYPES.filter((type) => new RegExp(`\\b${type}\\b`, 'i').test(beforeDash));
683: }
684: 
685: /**
686:  * Permanent subtypes a `permanentSubtype` qualifier can narrow to. A curated
687:  * constant rather than a full Scryfall subtype catalog fetch — that would be
688:  * an api-policy-gated change (see docs/api-policy.md) for a handful of
689:  * subtypes the corpus actually cares about.
690:  */
691: const PERMANENT_SUBTYPES = ['Vehicle', 'Equipment', 'Saga', 'Clue', 'Treasure', 'Food'];
692: 
693: function findPermanentSubtypes(typeLine: string): string[] {
694:   return PERMANENT_SUBTYPES.filter((subtype) => new RegExp(`\\b${subtype}\\b`, 'i').test(typeLine));
695: }
696: 
697: /** Keywords that are themselves an alternative cost, rather than text saying
698:  * so — Evoke (Walker of the Grove), Cleave (Lantern Flare), Delve (Empty the
699:  * Pits), Convoke (Vault Guardsman). */
700: const ALTERNATIVE_COST_KEYWORDS = ['Evoke', 'Cleave', 'Delve', 'Convoke'];
701: 
702: /**
703:  * The two self-referential templates Wizards uses for "you may cast this
704:  * spell for something other than its mana cost": Fierce Guardianship's
705:  * commander clause ("cast this spell without paying its mana cost") and the
706:  * pay-alternative template (Snuff Out, Thunderclap, Force of Despair,
707:  * "rather than pay this spell's mana cost"). Deliberately scoped to "this
708:  * spell" — Nissa, Worldsoul Speaker's "rather than pay the mana cost for
709:  * permanent spells you cast" reduces *other* spells' cost, which is
710:  * `enables` (`reducesCostOf`), not a property of Nissa herself.
711:  */
712: const SELF_ALTERNATIVE_COST_PATTERN =
713:   /\bcast this spell without paying its mana cost\b|\brather than pay(?:ing)? this spell'?s mana cost\b/i;
714: 
715: function hasAlternativeCost(text: string, manaCost: string | null, keywords: string[]): boolean {
716:   if (manaCost?.includes('/P')) return true;
717:   if (ALTERNATIVE_COST_KEYWORDS.some((keyword) => keywords.includes(keyword))) return true;
718:   return SELF_ALTERNATIVE_COST_PATTERN.test(text);
719: }
720: 
721: /** "Modified creature(s)/permanent(s)" and "is/was modified" — CR's umbrella
722:  * term for a permanent with a counter on it or an Equipment/Aura attached.
723:  * Excludes "these modified rules" (Booster Blitz's house-rule variant,
724:  * nothing to do with the Modified mechanic). */
725: const MODIFIED_PATTERN =
726:   /\bmodified (?:creatures?|permanents?)\b|\b(?:is|are|was|were|it'?s) modified\b/i;
727: 
728: /** An actual win condition ("you win the game"), not a mere prevention
729:  * effect. The Book of Exalted Deeds grants an Angel "you can't lose the game
730:  * and your opponents can't win the game" — a symmetric protection clause,
731:  * not a win condition for its own controller — so it correctly reads false
732:  * here despite archetypes.md naming it as an example. */
733: const ALTERNATE_WIN_PATTERN = /\byou win the game\b/i;
734: 
735: export function buildCardFacts(row: CardRow, vocab: Vocabulary): CardFacts {
736:   const rawText = row.oracle_text ?? '';
737:   const faceNames = faceNamesIn(row.name);
738:   const text = normalizeLordWording(
739:     stripReminderText(stripSelfReferences(rawText, ...faceNames, row.back_name ?? null)),
740:     vocab,
741:   );
742:   const typeLine = row.type_line ?? '';
743:   return {
744:     name: row.name,
745:     typeLine,
746:     text,
747:     rawText,
748:     creatureTypes: parseJsonArray(row.creature_types),
749:     keywords: parseJsonArray(row.keywords),
750:     producedTokenTypes: [
751:       ...new Set([...findProducedTokenTypes(text, vocab), ...findAmassedTypes(text, vocab)]),
752:     ],
753:     sacrificesItself: detectsSelfSacrifice(rawText, faceNames),
754:     growsItself: detectsSelfGrowth(rawText, faceNames),
755:     isLand: /\bLand\b/.test(typeLine),
756:     isEquipment: /\bEquipment\b/.test(typeLine),
757:     isAura: /\bAura\b/.test(typeLine),
758:     cardTypes: findCardTypes(typeLine),
759:     permanentSubtypes: findPermanentSubtypes(typeLine),
760:     counterKinds: findAllCounterKinds(text),
761:     cmc: row.cmc ?? 0,
762:     alternativeCost: hasAlternativeCost(text, row.mana_cost, parseJsonArray(row.keywords)),
763:     modified: MODIFIED_PATTERN.test(text),
764:     alternateWin: ALTERNATE_WIN_PATTERN.test(text),
765:   };
766: }

# CLAUDE.md

Guidance for Claude Code when working in `apps/commander-recommender/`.

## What this is

A Commander recommender: paste or upload a card list, get ranked Commander suggestions —
including Partner/Background pairs — with cited synergies, ban-list legality, and an estimated
Bracket. React 19 + Vite client (Zustand + TanStack Query/Table), Express 5 + better-sqlite3
server, no ORM. Card data is Scryfall's Oracle Cards bulk export, imported into SQLite at
build/deploy time — the running server never calls Scryfall live.

this app's own handoff document (moved here during the monorepo consolidation, file map kept
current) and covers the deeper "why" behind the stack choices, the scoring model, and known risk
areas in more depth than this file repeats. This file is about how to work in the code, not what
the code does. The root [`CLAUDE.md`](../../CLAUDE.md) covers workspace-wide commands and
conventions this file doesn't repeat.

/ `--filter mtg-recommender-server` from the repo root).

  `server/data/cards.sqlite`; required before `/api/recommend` returns anything but a 503. Needs
  network access; reuses a copy less than a week old unless run as `prepare-data:fresh`

- **`server/src/services/synergy.ts`** is the heart of the app: builds a `CollectionProfile` from
  the matched cards (color identity, creature types, keywords, oracle-text theme regexes), then

  reviewable catalog of what those roles and archetypes are _meant_ to mean, derived from twenty real
  decks, and it records which current behaviours are deliberate (so they don't get "fixed") and which
  are known gaps. `deckAnalysis.ts` + `lifecycle.ts` + `packages.ts`
  build on it to answer "what is this list trying to do, and what's it missing" independent of any
  commander — see `docs/commander-recommender.md`'s file map for how those three fit together.
